afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 112009
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
109 PM MST Fri Sep 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Extreme Heat Warnings continue across portions of Southeast 
  California and Southwest Arizona through this evening ahead of 
  slightly cooling temperatures through the weekend.

- Shower and thunderstorm chances will be focused mainly over the
  high terrain of Northern and Eastern Arizona over the next few 
  days before increasing coverage and spreading into the lower 
  deserts early next week.

- Near to slightly above normal temperatures are expected for 
  this weekend and likely through the first part of next week. 
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Saturday/...
Current upper-air analysis reveals flat ridging over the the Desert 
Southwest as troughing over the Pacific Northwest displaces the sub-
tropical high toward Southern Arizona and Northern Mexico. These 
clashing air masses have also translated to a bit of high 
pressure erosion which will result in some slightly "cooler" 
temperatures across across the region. However, the difference 
compared to the previous few days will not be incredibly 
noticeable, in fact, extreme heat conditions will continue through
at least this evening for portions of Southeast California and 
Southwest Arizona. Afternoon highs today over these areas will 
range between 105-111 degrees, but it will feel even hotter thanks
to abundant surface moisture. Apparent temperatures will range 
closer to 110-115 degrees as dew points hover in the lower to 
upper 60s. Elsewhere across the lower deserts, afternoon readings 
will run near 100-106 degrees, backing away from Major HeatRisk, 
but still around 5 degrees above normal for this time of year.

Although the expectation is that shower and thunderstorm activity 
will be focused over the high terrain areas of Northern and Eastern 
Arizona over the next few days, it is not out of the realm of 
possibility that some activity could sneak over parts of the lower 
deserts this evening/tonight. The two main factors that will 
determine if this comes to fruition are if a strong enough outflow
or colliding outflows from distant convection will occur and the 
timing of this potential outcome. The environment will be
favorable for convection this afternoon with forecast soundings 
indicating mixing ratios of 14 g/kg and ML CAPE values possibly 
near or exceeding 1500 J/kg. However, hi-res guidance is 
indicating that if outflows, providing the needed lift, were to 
approach population centers of Pinal and Maricopa Counties, it 
would not be until after sunset, at a time when instability would
be on the decrease while the cap rebuilds. Not to mention that 
anything that may fire up will also have to deal with synoptic 
subsidence due to the sub-tropical high. The bottom line is, 
lower elevation convection will be heavily conditional on how 
activity evolves elsewhere, and therefore, rain chances are only 
20-25% for areas such as the Phoenix metro tonight as a lot of 
uncertainty remains in the forecast. Further east over the 
foothill and mountainous areas, it is not surprise that slightly 
better chances (30-40%) for rain exist thanks to orographic 
influences.

As for Saturday, it appears that rain chances of backed off compared
to previous forecast runs. Tomorrow might be more of down day in 
terms of convection across most of the state, relative to what is 
expected this afternoon. With the high and associated subsidence 
still overhead, and the atmosphere likely to be worked over, 
thunderstorm coverage would likely be more isolated to a few spots
over The Rim and enhanced terrain features of Southeast Arizona. 
Even with a decent environment still in place with projected ML 
CAPE ~1200 J/kg and mixing rations ~13 g/kg, without a larger 
complex of convection sending organized outflows our way, there 
will be an absence of lift to spark more showers and storms 
downstream over the lower deserts of our forecast area. So far, 
the early hi-res runs favor this drier outcome. Regardless of how 
convection transpires, day-to-day temperatures will fall slightly,
with afternoon highs ranging between 99-108 degrees. HeatRisk 
levels will be in the Minor to Moderate category for most of the 
region, warranting the conclusion of this stretch of Extreme Heat 
products, but a few isolated spots of Major Heat Risk will linger,
mainly for the Imperial and Lower Colorado River Valleys.

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
As stated last night, forecast uncertainty remains quite high for
storm potential for the first part of next week. Guidance is in
good agreement with the synoptic set up for Sunday through early
next week, but it's the subtle mesoscale features that differ and
where the main uncertainty lies. Models are also in better
agreement with increasing moisture Sunday into Monday compared to
last night and this in turn is leading to higher forecast
instability and even PoPs. The ridge will continue to shift
farther to the east during this time as a trough moves into the
Northwestern U.S. The main shortwave within the trough will track
across the Northern Rockies, but the southern fringes of the 
trough is still likely to bring increased support for showers and
thunderstorms by early next week. Models show a seasonably strong
upper level jet setting up from the Northern Rockies through the 
Great Basin by Monday which is expected to place our region within
a favorable area for ascent as early as Sunday night and 
potentially lasting through next Tuesday or Wednesday. 

Other unknowns for early next week will be the placement of the 
best moisture and likely the small swatch of the best instability.
It seems likely there will be considerable cloudiness somewhere 
over or near eastern Arizona which will limit instability, while
the best instability/lower CIN sets up in a more cloud-free area 
to the west (South-central AZ). There is also a decent chance of 
having some sort of mesoscale disturbance tracking northward out 
of Mexico at some point early next week which will help to 
initiate storm activity. However, uncertainty is still too high to
be able to pinpoint the timing and the potential for storms, but 
there is more optimism for at least one or two busy storm days 
early next week. NBM PoPs have increased for early next week and 
look fairly reasonable at anywhere from 30-70% across south- 
central and eastern Arizona. If moisture and instability ends up 
on the higher end of guidance, we are likely to have to worry 
about some strong storms and heavy rainfall/flooding potential. 
How long this increased rain potential may last is also uncertain 
as models really don't change the synoptic set up through at least
next Thursday or Friday. It's doubtful we will have good rain 
chances each day next week, but it also seems likely there will 
not be any strong drying that will affect the area.

Temperatures next week are almost as uncertain as rain chances as
fairly high model spread is seen from Sunday-Wednesday, but with
at least a downtrend in temperatures. The latter half of next week
shows even higher spread, but with an uptrend in temperatures with
readings eventually warming back to above normal by next weekend.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1757Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 

The only aviation weather issue will be gusty afternoon/late 
evening gusts, with the possibility of a distant TS outflow 
causing sudden gusty winds out of the SE. Occasional afternoon 
gusts to between 15-20 kts are likely with gusts expected to be 
increase to between 20-25kts between 04-06Z. Chances for TSRA/SHRA
directly impacting the terminals are too low (10% or less) to 
include in the TAF late afternoon/evening, however a few hours of 
VCSH have been introduced from 06-11Z. FEW- SCT and at times BKN 
mid and high cloud decks will persist through the period.

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:

Winds will continue to oscillate between SE and SW at KIPL with 
speeds peaking between 8 to 15 kts sustained. KBLH will maintain a
southerly flow with speeds aoa 10kts and gusts between 20-25kt,
gusts will relax for the overnight period, however sustained
speeds will remain aoa 10kts. The possibility of another distant 
TS outflow reaching KIPL cannot be ruled out late this afternoon/early
evening. Periods with FEW- SCT and occasionally BKN mid and high 
cloud decks will continue. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Above normal temperatures will continue into the weekend, but 
with some gradual cooling as humidities remain somewhat elevated. 
Isolated chances for showers and a few thunderstorms can be 
expected through the weekend, with the best chances over the 
Arizona high terrain. Rain chances should improve during the first
half of next week with temperatures eventually dipping to around
average for mid September. MinRHs through early next week will 
generally be between 15-25% across the western districts and 
25-35% across the eastern districts. Winds will somewhat follow
typical diurnal patterns, but with more of a south southwesterly
predominant wind across the western districts. Daily afternoon
gusts of 20-25 mph will be common across the Lower CO River
Valley through the weekend before becoming more widespread early
next week.

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST this evening for AZZ530-532-
     533.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT this evening for CAZ562-566-
     567-569-570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...RW
LONG TERM...Kuhlman
AVIATION...Ryan
FIRE WEATHER...Kuhlman
